prompt.adult: Paul left Titus behind to set in order what was lacking and to appoint elders in every city. Where did he leave him?
prompt.child: Paul gave Titus a job: to set the churches in order and appoint leaders. On what island did he leave Titus?
prompt.teen: Titus 1:5: “For this reason I left you in” where?
prompt.older: According to Titus 1:5, where did Paul leave Titus?

verses.text: For this reason I left you in Crete, that you should set in order the things that are lacking, and appoint elders in every city as I commanded you—

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 5.
explanation.teen: 1:5 says where Titus was left, then two tasks. Read the place.
explanation.older: It follows “For this reason I left you in” in 1:5.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:5 says Titus was to appoint elders in every city. 1:4 calls Titus a true son in our common faith.

prompt.adult: Paul planned to send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus. Where did he want Titus to come to him, because he had decided to spend the winter there?
prompt.child: Paul wanted Titus to meet him for the winter. Where?
prompt.teen: Titus 3:12: “be diligent to come to me at” where?
prompt.older: According to Titus 3:12, where was Paul planning to spend the winter?

verses.text: When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.

explanation.child: Look right after “come to me at” in verse 12.
explanation.teen: 3:12 names two men Paul may send, then where Titus should come, then why. Read the place.
explanation.older: It follows “be diligent to come to me at” in 3:12.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:12 names Artemas and Tychicus. 3:13 asks Titus to send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey with haste.
teaching.takeaway: Paul planned to winter at Nicopolis.

prompt.adult: 2:7 tells Titus to show himself a pattern of good works. According to 2:8, why should his speech be sound and beyond condemnation?
prompt.child: Paul tells Titus to set a good example and speak in a way no one can fault. What would happen to anyone who opposed him?
prompt.teen: Titus 2:8: “that one who is an opponent may be” what?
prompt.older: According to Titus 2:8, what will become of an opponent when Titus’ speech is sound?

verses.text: in all things showing yourself to be a pattern of good works; in doctrine showing integrity, reverence, incorruptibility,
sound speech that cannot be condemned, that one who is an opponent may be ashamed, having nothing evil to say of you.

explanation.child: Look right after “may be” in verse 8.
explanation.teen: 2:7 speaks of a pattern; 2:8 names sound speech, then what happens to an opponent, then why. Read the middle.
explanation.older: It follows “that one who is an opponent may be” in 2:8.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:7 names integrity, reverence, and incorruptibility in doctrine. 2:1 tells Titus to speak what is proper for sound doctrine.
teaching.takeaway: Sound speech leaves an opponent ashamed.

prompt.adult: 3:9 tells Titus to avoid foolish disputes, genealogies, and strivings about the law. According to 3:10, when should he reject a divisive man?
prompt.child: Paul tells Titus to avoid pointless arguments. In 3:10, when should Titus reject a person who keeps causing division?
prompt.teen: Titus 3:10: “Reject a divisive man after” what?
prompt.older: According to Titus 3:10, after what should a divisive man be rejected?

choices.text: a hearing before all the church
a full year of quiet waiting
a vote of all the elders

verses.text: But avoid foolish disputes, genealogies, contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and useless.
Reject a divisive man after the first and second admonition,

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 10.
explanation.teen: 3:9 lists what to avoid; 3:10 names whom to reject and after what. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “Reject a divisive man after” in 3:10.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:9 says those disputes are unprofitable and useless. 3:11 says such a person is warped and sinning.
teaching.takeaway: Reject a divisive man after the first and second admonition.

prompt.adult: 2:14 says He gave Himself for us to redeem us from every lawless deed. In 2:13, what are we looking for, along with the glorious appearing of our great God and Savior?
prompt.child: Paul says Jesus gave Himself to free us from wrongdoing. What does 2:13 say believers are looking forward to?
prompt.older: Read with 2:14, what does 2:13 say we are looking for?

verses.text: looking for the blessed hope and glorious appearing of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ,
who gave Himself for us, that He might redeem us from every lawless deed and purify for Himself His own special people, zealous for good works.

explanation.adult: Read the words after “looking for” in 2:13.
explanation.child: Look right after “looking for” in verse 13.
explanation.teen: 2:14 says what He gave and why; 2:13 names two things we look for, then whose appearing. Read the first.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:14 says He purifies for Himself His own special people, zealous for good works. 2:11 says the grace of God has appeared to all men.
teaching.takeaway: We look for the blessed hope and glorious appearing.

prompt.adult: 2:11 says the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared, and 3:4 says the kindness of God our Savior toward man appeared. In 3:5, through what did He save us, according to His mercy?
prompt.child: Paul says God’s kindness has appeared to us. According to 3:5, through what did God save us?
prompt.older: Linking 2:11 and 3:4, through what does 3:5 say He saved us?

choices.text: the keeping of the whole law
the blood of bulls and goats

verses.text: For the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men,
But when the kindness and the love of God our Savior toward man appeared,
not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to His mercy He saved us, through the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Spirit,

explanation.child: Look right after “He saved us, through” in verse 5.
explanation.teen: 3:4 says what appeared; 3:5 says what did not save us, what did, and then through what. Read the last part.
explanation.older: It follows “according to His mercy He saved us, through” in 3:5.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:5 says it was not by works of righteousness which we have done. 3:6 says He poured out the Spirit on us abundantly.
teaching.takeaway: He saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Spirit.

prompt.adult: 3:7 speaks of becoming heirs, justified by His grace. In 1:2, how does Paul describe the God who promised before time began?
prompt.child: Paul says believers will inherit what God promised. In 1:2, what does he say about the God who made that promise?
prompt.teen: Titus 1:2: what does Paul say about God, who “promised before time began”?
prompt.older: Read with 3:7, how does 1:2 describe the God who made the promise?

verses.text: in hope of eternal life which God, who cannot lie, promised before time began,
that having been justified by His grace we should become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

explanation.child: Look right after the word “God” in verse 2.
explanation.teen: 3:7 speaks of heirs; 1:2 names the hope, then describes God, then when He promised. Read the description.
explanation.older: It comes between “which God,” and “promised” in 1:2.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:3 says He has in due time manifested His word through preaching. 3:7 says we have been justified by His grace.
teaching.takeaway: God, who cannot lie, promised before time began.

prompt.adult: In 1:4 Paul calls Titus a true son. In 2:15, with what is Titus to speak, exhort, and rebuke?
prompt.child: Paul treats Titus like a son. In 2:15, how does Paul tell Titus to speak, exhort, and rebuke?
prompt.teen: Titus 2:15: “Speak these things, exhort, and rebuke with” what?
prompt.older: Beside 1:4, what does 2:15 say Titus should rebuke with?

verses.text: To Titus, a true son in our common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior.
Speak these things, exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no one despise you.

explanation.child: Look right after “rebuke with” in verse 15.
explanation.teen: 1:4 greets Titus; 2:15 gives three commands, says with what, and then a warning. Read the middle.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:15 ends, “Let no one despise you.” 1:4 sends grace, mercy, and peace.
teaching.takeaway: Titus was to rebuke with all authority.
